lines.text: {winner} has the overall title, and I'd rather have that than the most convincing argument in the pub.

lines.text: Measured across the whole challenge, {winnerClub} ended {margin} ahead. It's not a snapshot, it's the complete picture.

lines.text: Credit {loser} with a challenge worth overcoming. A title means more when the opposition has earned respect.

lines.text: Funny thing about a season medal, you can polish it forever. An overall title settles the bigger question.
Listen, nobody gets this far by accident. {winner} has earned the final word.
For {loserClub}, it's a disappointing outcome, certainly. It isn't a reason to dismiss their entire campaign.
lines.was: For {loserClub}, there will be plenty to take forward, just not the Showdown title this time.

lines.text: Quite a tidy conclusion, really. All that friendly disagreement has produced a proper sporting answer.
lines.was: Quite a tidy conclusion, really. Months of friendly disagreement reduced to a proper sporting answer.

lines.text: Think beyond the last result. Winning the entire contest is about what survives after every season is counted.

lines.text: Amazing how quickly the banter changes when the overall champion is finally known.

lines.text: Sometimes you need to put the individual souvenirs away before you can appreciate the size of the overall prize.
lines.was: Sometimes you need the full campaign to know who has done the better job. Now we know.

lines.text: That familiar argument over who had the better run has just found a permanent answer.
Consider the sort of achievement that still sounds impressive after the excitement has died down. This qualifies.

lines.text: Give the other manager some credit. A victory feels more substantial when the opposition was worth facing.

lines.was: Nobody's taking away the effort on either side. The overall prize still has a single owner.

lines.text: That's the thing people overlook, you can own a wonderful chapter without owning the book.

lines.text: Try winning a single season and you get applause. Win the entire thing and you get the bragging rights.

lines.was: Different chapters, same competition, and {winner} has written the ending that counts.

lines.text: A manager can have fine moments and still fall short. {winner} collected the bigger reward.

Careful with any jokes at {loser}'s expense. A worthy opponent makes the achievement matter.

lines.text: Instead of arguing over each chapter, you can finally judge the book as a whole.

lines.text: Good to see {winner} do the unglamorous part as well, staying competitive until there was nothing left to contest.
lines.was: Good to see {winner} finish the job. Finishing it is the part people tend to underestimate.

lines.text: {loser} made the winner work for the recognition, which makes this a proper sporting finish.

lines.text: If you're {loserClub}, you'll want another opportunity. That's the attitude that gives a rivalry its future.

lines.text: It's the entire run that earns this honor. You can't just freeze the table at a flattering moment.

lines.text: Nice to see {winner} with {margin} to spare at the finish. That's more satisfying than a promising position.

lines.text: That is the danger with judging a long competition by a snapshot. The frame misses everything around it.
lines.was: That is a useful reminder, a great individual moment and a great overall achievement aren't interchangeable.

lines.text: Discussions about individual seasons will continue, naturally. The title itself isn't under discussion anymore.
lines.was: Plenty of room for friendly debate later. Not much room to dispute the overall winner.

lines.text: Success at this level asks you to hold your own across the journey, not merely enjoy a good spell.
If you ask {loser}, they'll likely recall favorite moments. {winner} can settle for the overall honor.
lines.was: Well, {loser} can keep the best anecdotes. {winner} gets to keep the title.

lines.text: There's your ending. No extra chapter needed, because the Showdown belongs to {winner}.
Not much to add once the contest is complete. That's the advantage of a proper conclusion.
Some trophies look grand in a picture. {winner} has claimed something better, an answer to the whole challenge.
lines.was: Some victories give you a pleasant memory. This gives {winner} the whole rivalry's bragging rights.

lines.text: No generous rival can seriously dispute that {winner} has won the entire Showdown.
lines.was: Even the most generous rival has to concede that {winner} is the overall champion.

lines.text: With the entire rivalry settled, nobody has to wonder which achievement outweighs which.

lines.was: I'll give {loser} this much, the opponent's achievement looks better for having faced them.

lines.text: You can put each campaign under a microscope, but the ultimate prize demands the widest possible view.
lines.was: You can admire each chapter separately, but the closing page is where the whole contest gets judged.

lines.text: Quite a finish, and not because of any single twist. The whole competition has finally delivered its champion.
lines.was: A proper finish, that. The competition has its champion, and the rivalry has another story.

lines.text: Hardly the time for a long explanation. A title across the entire competition explains itself.

lines.was: You see why the overall contest matters. It rewards the manager who finishes with the most.

lines.text: Settling the friendly rivalry gives both managers a fresh subject for endless conversation.
lines.was: Funny how the end of the rivalry also gives it fresh material for all the old jokes.

lines.text: Enough has been decided for {winner} to put the controllers down with an unusually satisfied expression.
lines.was: Enough has been decided for {winner} to put the debate away, at least for tonight.

lines.text: For {loserClub}, pride in taking part can sit comfortably beside the disappointment of finishing second.

lines.text: Remember, the imagined highlight reel doesn't choose the champion. The completed competition does.
lines.was: Remember, a result can look impressive in isolation. An overall title has to stand up to the lot.

lines.text: Hard to add much about {winner}. The difficult bit wasn't the closing scene, it was earning that scene.
lines.was: Hard to improve on that from {winner}. You can only win the Showdown that was put before you.

lines.text: After the closing whistle, there isn't another step on the ladder. You can only look at who finished highest.
lines.was: After the closing whistle on the wider contest, you can admire the effort without reopening the decision.

lines.text: Plenty of smaller triumphs will be remembered, but they're all part of the story of who finished first.
Try choosing a favorite memory if you like. {winnerPoints} to {loserPoints} is how the campaign is judged.
lines.was: Imagine trying to pick the best single memory. Happily, the overall result doesn't ask you to do that.

lines.text: Whatever {loser} takes from this, a finished series doesn't erase the good moments along the way.
lines.was: From {loser}'s side, the next contest may bring a fresh answer. This one's already decided.

lines.text: A full Showdown asks for more than a flourish, and the winners have supplied an answer.
A trophy shelf has room for memories, but this is the sort of honor that deserves its own space.
Put it in the cabinet for {winner}. That's the reward for coming out ahead overall.
Nothing left to negotiate now, unlike those endless arguments about whose favorite season was better.
lines.was: Nothing to protest about the final whistle now. The contest has finished with a champion.

lines.text: Entire campaigns are remembered by their final standing. This one has found its champion.
I'll wager {loser} has favorite memories from this, even if the ultimate prize went elsewhere.
lines.was: I'll wager {loser} remembers a few brilliant moments. They don't alter who takes this title.

lines.text: Congratulations to {winner}, of course, but give the entire friendly competition its due as well.
lines.was: At this stage, the only sensible thing is to congratulate {winner} and admire the rivalry.

lines.text: {winnerClub} takes the contest by {margin} overall. Individual seasons had their turns, and now comes the bigger honor.

lines.text: The next argument might begin soon, but {winner} has a rather useful answer tucked away.
lines.was: The next argument might begin tomorrow, but {winner} has won the one that just ended.

lines.text: If {winner} smiles for a while, nobody should be surprised. That's a substantial achievement.
Not every stretch has to be pretty. You need enough quality when all the seasons are taken together.
lines.was: Not every stretch of this contest needed to be perfect. The finished outcome needed to be better.

lines.text: {loserClub} hasn't claimed the title, but its place in a serious rivalry is beyond question.
lines.was: {loserClub} has lost the overall contest, not its standing as a worthy opponent.

lines.text: It's the simplest explanation of a complicated rivalry, really. {winner} finished on top.
Reaching the end is not the same as reaching it on top. That's why this honor matters.
Behind all the banter was a real test, and {winnerClub} has come out the stronger overall.
There's no clever alternative reading of the final result. The whole Showdown goes to {winner}.
{loser} can take the final laugh, if they like. {winner} has rather more to smile about.

lines.text: What matters is the full body of work, and {winnerClub} has been the best over that distance.
lines.was: The contest demanded patience as well as results. {winnerClub} has been rewarded at the end.

lines.text: What {winner} has won here can't be undone by a clever retelling of earlier seasons.

lines.was: It's not always the loudest achievement that carries the furthest. The overall title does.

lines.text: {winnerClub} has won the Showdown. Everything else now belongs in the stories told afterward.

Rather than prepare a speech, {winner} could just frame {winnerPoints} to {loserPoints}. Efficient, really.

lines.text: Those accumulated points have done their job for {winner}. The reward is the overall title.
lines.was: Those points over the entire contest have delivered {winner} the prize that matters most.

lines.text: Right then, the debate can take a holiday. {winnerClub} is the finished Showdown's champion.
{winner} now gets to enjoy that rare luxury, a sporting argument with an actual conclusion.
At the closing whistle, it's not the loudest memory that matters. It's the name engraved at the end.
lines.was: All the individual seasons have had their say, and the final word belongs to the champion.

lines.text: {loser} hasn't been written out of the story. Their challenge is part of what made it memorable.

lines.was: The final page looks rather good for {winnerClub}. A proper ending after a proper contest.

lines.text: Banter will carry on as ever, except {winner} can now point to the finished standings.

lines.text: {loserClub} has reason to come back with ambition. A gracious ending doesn't mean the rivalry is finished.
